title: Widget of control audio/video in web browser thumbnails shown in all instead of one
line: With task grouping off, only the window that is playing media shows the media controls and album art in its tooltip.
explanation: Tooltips decide which window gets the media controls by checking whether a window title contains the playing track (hasTrackInATitle), but that check only ran inside group tooltips. With grouping off each window has its own single tooltip, which never set hasTrackInATitle and fell back to index 0, so every window of the player's process showed the controls and, for non-browsers, the album art. The single tooltip now computes hasTrackInATitle over the task model's windows with the same PID, and the controls, volume row and album art use the title match when it is set.

commits.message:
applets/taskmanager: show media controls only on the playing window

With grouping off, every window of a player's app got the media controls
and album art in its tooltip, as the window title check only ran for
group tooltips. Single tooltips now look at the app's other windows too.

BUG: 455654

media.caption: Master, grouping off: two windows of one player app; 'Page One' also shows the playback controls
Fixed: only the window whose title has the track shows the controls
Master, player with album art: art and controls on both windows
Fixed: 'Page One' shows its own thumbnail; art and controls only on the playing window

reviews.text: Clean, well-reasoned fix in Task Manager tooltips that extends the track-in-title check (hasTrackInATitle) to single-window tooltips across tasks sharing the same PID, restricting media controls, volume controls, and album art to the playing window when grouping is off. Switching the controls' active check from albumArtImage.available to root.titleIncludesTrack also fixes controls disappearing when a player provides no album art, while keeping the fallback intact when no window title matches (e.g. a background browser tab). Before/after screenshots clearly verify both art and non-art cases.

The cause is right: hasTrackInATitle was only computed for group tooltips, so with grouping off every single tooltip fell back to index 0 and every window of the player's process got the controls. Computing it over the same-PID top-level tasks (the PID the MPRIS lookup already uses) applies the title-match rule Adam proposed and Nate agreed to in c7-c8, and the speaker badge part of c0 is rightly left to bug 375943, as the confirming comment split it. Because the tooltip Loader is recreated on each show, the non-reactive tasksModel.data() reads won't go stale in practice. Before/after screenshots from the fake two-window MPRIS app show controls and art only on the matching window. Nit: the commit message doesn't mention that group tooltips now show controls on the matching window even when the player has no album art; worth one line for the reviewer.
